reason: C best balances atmosphere, task emphasis and enlarged-text composition on both screens. Ask prioritizes the question while retaining visible identity context. Why gives evidence categories readable full-width rows and a dedicated reader with explicit return navigation. These are provisional composition winners, not verified functional replacements or acceptance passes.
limitations: Feedback is N/A for all screen interaction grades: the numeric schema cannot represent N/A, so feedback: 0 is an encoding placeholder, not a failing score. It is excluded from every calculation. Component tuples use N/A directly. F and overall therefore summarize only observed clarity/accessibility and are incomplete functional assessments.
Only attached images and the user-supplied evidence boundaries were considered. No source, previous grades, other graders or additional files were inspected.

Component tuple order is hierarchy, typography/spacing, surfaces/color, clarity, feedback/recovery, accessibility. Component accessibility scores assess visible layout only. Shared prototype headers score [7,7,8,7,N/A,6]: the close glyph is visually tiny, and its actual hit area is unverified. Baseline header scores [7,7,8,6,N/A,7], with Plus · test adding unrelated emphasis.

Production's reported browser checks and working readings/export belong to baseline alone. Prototype control drives establish structural operability and content reachability, not submission, engine integration, export or runtime recovery.

A/B Ask bottom-action overlap is a visible composition concern; supplied reachability evidence prevents concluding that content or controls are inaccessible. No demonstrated hard-gate failure is established by these captures.

Prototype implementation requirements: real submission and engine wiring; empty/invalid/loading/error/success states; preserved question and identity across navigation; keyboard-safe scrolling and action placement; visible focus, semantic labels/selection/disclosure state, focus restoration, measured contrast and 44pt targets; reduced-motion behavior and export where applicable.

Why A/B need enlarged-text navigation that does not split category names mid-word. Why C still needs verified reader navigation, focus/scroll restoration and return behavior. No expanded Ask C identity view is supplied.
The synthetic reasoning fixture was assessed for layout and navigation only. Repetition was not treated as model quality or rewarded through hidden/shorter content.

No composition demonstrates A>=9 and F>=9 for every screen and meaningful component. Physical iPhone/VoiceOver, native voice, keyboard and haptics remain separate unverified gates; their absence did not impose a blanket browser-score ceiling.
